# First freeze check: extractor recall on independently seeded plans (2026-11-15)

Context for a reader with no history: the Sweep Sheet design relies on a script pre-pass (extractors E1 to E7) that finds, in a plan, the places where a defect of a given class (C1 to C8) can hide. The design's freeze gate (REQ-21, test `tests/test_recall.py`, marker `freeze`) requires recall of at least 0.8 for E1, E2, E3, E4 and E7 on plans in which a second author, who had not read the extractors, seeded defects. See `../OPEN-ITEMS.md` and `../../OPEN-QUESTIONS-20261115.md`.

## What was run

- Fixtures: `fixtures/recall/` written by a fresh Sonnet session (not a person) on 2026-11-15: 4 real plans, 37 seeds (C1 5, C2 7, C4 6, C5 5, C6 6, C7 7, C8 1). Report: `second-author-report/REPORT.md`. The session did not run any extractor.
- Command: `uv run --frozen --project <repo> pytest -p no:cacheprovider <SW>/tests -q -m freeze`.

## Result: the gate FAILS

| Extractor | Class | Seeds found / seeded | Recall (gate 0.8) | Candidates produced, how many hit a seed (precision) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| E1 | C1, C6 | 2 / 11 | 0.18 | 2 of 60 (0.03) |
| E2 | C4 | 3 / 6 | 0.50 | 52 of 220 (0.24) |
| E3 | C8 | 0 / 1 | 0.00 | 0 of 0 |
| E4 | C5 | 1 / 5 | 0.20 | 1 of 47 (0.02) |
| E7 | C7 | 0 / 7 | 0.00 | 0 of 6 |
| E6 (experimental, not gated) | C3 | no seeds | n/a | 0 of 45 |
| E5 (needs source) | C2 | not in the gated list | n/a | 0 of 0 |

The other freeze test, the lint against the real ground-truth files, fails only because `LINT_REAL_GT_GLOB` is not set (it was not run).

## How to read it (and what is not known)

- **The result is real but not yet a verdict on the design.** The extractors were built from the design's description of defect shapes and tested here for the first time against defects someone else wrote. Low recall means the shapes the extractors recognise do not match how independent seeds are phrased, or that the seeds are not the kind of defect the extractors target. This note does not say which.
- **E2 to E4 ran without a repository snapshot.** The test contract searches the repository only if `fixtures/recall/<plan>/snapshot/` exists; the second author did not provide one (the instruction did not require it). Evidence-searching extractors therefore had no tree to search. This depresses E2, E3 and E4 and is a fixture gap, not an extractor result. E1 and E7 do not depend on a snapshot, and they scored 0.18 and 0.00.
- **C8 has one seed**, so its recall figure means nothing.
- **Matching is strict:** a candidate counts only if its class equals the seed's and its anchor text contains the quote or is contained in it.
- **Class labels of seeds can be ambiguous** (the second author notes some seeds fit two classes).
- **Nothing has been tuned.** No extractor was changed after seeing this result. Tuning extractors to these four plans is allowed by the design (they are not hold-out documents) but would risk overfitting four plans; the hold-out test later is the real check.

## Options for the owner

1. **Diagnose, then fix the fixtures first:** add `snapshot/` checkouts to the recall plans (pre-implementation commits of each plan), add C8 seeds, and re-run. This isolates how much of the failure is the missing snapshot.
2. **Then iterate the extractors** on three of the four plans and test on the fourth (train/test split), with the second author re-seeding at least one new plan for a fresh check; re-run the gate.
3. **Stop the Sweep Sheet** if recall stays far below 0.8 after fair fixes, and rely on the Recipe Ledger (which has no extractor). Report this as the finding.

Nothing is committed. The freeze, the tag and the hash list wait on this.
=======
# Authors of the recall fixtures (F-RECALL, REQ-21)

## Who seeded

A fresh Claude Code session, not a person. Model: claude-sonnet-5-5. Date: 2026-11-15 (UTC).
The session was started only for this task (plan step 14.1).

## What the author had and had not read

The author had **not** read the extractors or any ground truth. Specifically, the session did not open, list the contents of or run anything that prints: `sweep/*.py`, `analysis/*.py`, `scaffold/*.py`, `tests/test_e*.py`, `tests/test_recall.py`, `tests/test_g0.py`, any `ground-truth*.json` or `score*.json`, `results/`, `runs/`, the older evaluation workspaces (`20261111-a1`, `20261113-collab`, `20261114-recipe-ledger`), `.dev/reflect/`, `.dev/brainstorms/`, or the three study packages. It did not run pytest on the `freeze` marker or on any extractor, so it never saw which seeds are found.

What it did read: `TESTING.md` section 2 (F-RECALL), requirements REQ-21 and REQ-08, `DESIGN.md` only for the class names, `cards/*.json`, `cards/README.md`, `tests/test_cards.py`, `tests/test_readme.py`, the four plans below with their `source.md`, and a few repository files (tests, `install_skill.py`, `src/` file names) to confirm that a seed points at something real.

## Plans

| Plan id (package folder under `.dev/tasks/done/`) | Seeds |
|---|---|
| `TASK-WF-diagnosticRefres-20261109-144413` | 7 |
| `TASK-WF-devGuideRefactor-20261104-135403` | 12 |
| `TASK-WF-removeTheAnyIssu-20261102-053741` | 11 |
| `TASK-WF-renameTheScIssue-20261104-174359` | 7 |

None is one of the three study packages (`TASK-WF-designSpec-20261107-075614`, `TASK-WF-makeTheAliasOnly-20261105-051649`, `TASK-WF-design-20261108-041415`). The plan `TASK-WF-launcherFollowup-20261105-131531` was read and dropped because its source points into a study package.

Seeds per class (37 in all): C1 5, C2 7, C4 6, C5 5, C6 6, C7 7, C8 1. Class C3 is not seeded (it is not in the list for this fixture).

## Overlap caveat

The author cannot know the hold-out documents or the planted-set plans. **Overlap of these four plans with the hold-out set was not checked.** If any of them is a hold-out or planted-set document, drop that folder before the freeze.

## Other limits to know

- Class C8 has one seed only. A seed for it needs an edited file that a test elsewhere pins and that the plan never names or runs; only one such pin could be confirmed in the repository as it was before the plan ran, so the C8 recall figure rests on one seed.
- The plans are real and finished, and the repository is now at a later state than the plans' base commit, so a few repository facts a reviewer sees differ from what the plan assumed. Each seed was written to be visible from the plan text (or its source) alone; the description says what the wrong outcome is.
- The original plans carry real defects of their own. The seeds are additions, so a reviewer may also report defects that are in `original.md`; those count against precision, not recall.
- Each seed is an edit of the plan text. A seed that removes text is quoted at the sentence where the missing text should have been. Every quote in `seeds.json` occurs exactly once in `seeded.md` (checked by script, outside the repository, before this file was written).
- Some seeds fit two classes (for example, a criterion wider than its instruction is also one that cannot pass). The class in `seeds.json` is the author's one chosen label.

Files per plan folder: `original.md` (byte copy of the plan), `seeded.md`, `seeds.json` (id, class, quote, description), `source.md` (byte copy of the driving source).

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# build-sandbox.sh [--raw] [--packages FILE] <doc>   (DESIGN 11.2 H3 and H4, DD-15, section 10 row 7)
# Builds SB/<doc>/repo (the document's base snapshot) and SB/cand/<doc>/{candidate.md,source.md}.
#   --raw       arm Z0-raw: SB/<doc>/repo-raw, repository HEAD minus ground-truth files and .dev/eval-workspaces.
#   --packages  test hook: another packages file; accepted only under /tmp/.
# Exit 0: built, or already valid. Exit 2: invalid (E_SANDBOX_DIRTY, E_LEAK, E_BASE or a failed step).
# Git is read on SRC_REPO (archive, cat-file, show, rev-parse) and written only inside the throwaway
# sandbox directory SBT, always as "git -C $SBT ..." (K5; the check of Task 8 greps bin/ for any other form).
# Test overrides (SW_SB_ROOT, SW_SRC_REPO) are refused by bin/common.sh unless they point under /tmp/.
set -u -o pipefail
source "$(dirname "$0")/common.sh"

usage() {
  echo "usage: build-sandbox.sh [--raw] [--packages FILE] <doc>" >&2
  exit 2
}
RAW=0
PKFILE=$SW/config/packages.json
DOC=
while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
  case "$1" in
    --raw) RAW=1 ;;
    --packages)
      shift
      [ $# -gt 0 ] || usage
      PKFILE=$1
      ;;
    -*) usage ;;
    *)
      [ -z "$DOC" ] || usage
      DOC=$1
      ;;
  esac
  shift
done
[ -n "$DOC" ] || usage
[[ $DOC =~ ^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._-]*$ ]] || { echo "E_DOC: bad document id: $DOC" >&2; exit 2; }
if [ "$PKFILE" != "$SW/config/packages.json" ]; then
  case "$(realpath -m -- "$PKFILE")/" in
    /tmp/?*) ;;
    *) echo "E_OVERRIDE: --packages $PKFILE is outside /tmp/" >&2; exit 2 ;;
  esac
fi
[ -f "$PKFILE" ] || { echo "E_PACKAGES: $PKFILE not found" >&2; exit 2; }
jq -e --arg p "$DOC" '.packages[$p]' "$PKFILE" >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "unknown package $DOC" >&2; exit 2; }

BASE=$(jq -r --arg p "$DOC" '.packages[$p].base // empty' "$PKFILE")
CAND_REL=$(jq -r --arg p "$DOC" '.packages[$p].candidate // empty' "$PKFILE")
SRC_REL=$(jq -r --arg p "$DOC" '.packages[$p].source // empty' "$PKFILE")
mapfile -t MASKED < <(jq -r --arg p "$DOC" '.packages[$p].masked_paths // [] | .[]' "$PKFILE")
mapfile -t IDS < <(jq -r '.packages | keys[]' "$PKFILE")

D=$SB/$DOC
if [ "$RAW" = 1 ]; then SUB=repo-raw META=sandbox-raw.json; else SUB=repo META=sandbox.json; fi
TARGET=$D/$SUB
SBT=$D/$SUB.tmp # the temporary sandbox directory; the only place a git write may happen
sw_assert_writable "$D" || exit 2
sw_assert_writable "$SB/cand/$DOC" || exit 2

# KIND: commit (a base commit, read with git archive), tree (a recorded working tree), raw (HEAD, DD-15)
TREEDIR=
if [ "$RAW" = 1 ]; then
  KIND=raw
  BASE=$(git -C "$SRC_REPO" rev-parse --verify -q 'HEAD^0') || { echo "E_BASE: no HEAD in $SRC_REPO" >&2; exit 2; }
elif [ -z "$BASE" ]; then
  echo "E_BASE: package $DOC has no base" >&2
  exit 2
elif [ "${BASE#tree:}" != "$BASE" ]; then
  KIND=tree
  TREEDIR=${BASE#tree:}
  case "$TREEDIR" in /*) ;; *) TREEDIR=$SRC_REPO/$TREEDIR ;; esac
  [ -d "$TREEDIR" ] || { echo "E_BASE: tree directory missing: $TREEDIR" >&2; exit 2; }
else
  KIND=commit
  git -C "$SRC_REPO" rev-parse --verify -q "$BASE^0" >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "E_BASE: $BASE is not a commit in $SRC_REPO" >&2; exit 2; }
fi

base_has() { # does the base hold path $1
  if [ "$KIND" = tree ]; then [ -e "$TREEDIR/$1" ]; else git -C "$SRC_REPO" cat-file -e "$BASE:$1" 2>/dev/null; fi
}
base_same() { # is file $2 the base version of path $1
  if [ "$KIND" = tree ]; then
    cmp -s -- "$TREEDIR/$1" "$2"
  else
    cmp -s <(git -C "$SRC_REPO" show "$BASE:$1" 2>/dev/null) "$2"
  fi
}
masked_ok() { # $1 = sandbox directory: each masked path is the base version, or absent where the base has none (REQ-03)
  local f
  [ "$RAW" = 1 ] && return 0
  for f in "${MASKED[@]}"; do
    if base_has "$f"; then
      base_same "$f" "$1/$f" || { echo "masked path differs from base: $f" >&2; return 1; }
    else
      [ ! -e "$1/$f" ] || { echo "masked path present but absent at base: $f" >&2; return 1; }
    fi
  done
}
leak_check() { # $1 = sandbox directory; any finding makes the sandbox invalid (REQ-04, REQ-34)
  local d=$1 bad=0 out id p
  out=$(cd "$d" && find . -path ./.git -prune -o -name 'ground-truth*' -print -quit)
  [ -z "$out" ] || { echo "E_LEAK: ground-truth file remains: $out" >&2; bad=1; }
  [ ! -e "$d/.dev/eval-workspaces" ] || { echo "E_LEAK: .dev/eval-workspaces remains" >&2; bad=1; }
  if [ "$RAW" != 1 ]; then
    for p in .dev/reflect .dev/tasks/done .dev/research; do
      [ ! -e "$d/$p" ] || { echo "E_LEAK: $p remains" >&2; bad=1; }
    done
    out=$(cd "$d" && find . -path ./.git -prune -o \( \( -name artifacts -type d \) -o -name progress.md \) -print -quit)
    [ -z "$out" ] || { echo "E_LEAK: artifacts or progress.md remains: $out" >&2; bad=1; }
    for id in "${IDS[@]}"; do
      out=$(cd "$d" && find . -path ./.git -prune -o -path "*$id*" -print -quit)
      [ -z "$out" ] || { echo "E_LEAK: path with document id remains: $out" >&2; bad=1; }
    done
    out=$(cd "$d" && grep -rIl --exclude-dir=.git -F -- "$DOC" . | head -n 3)
    [ -z "$out" ] || { echo "E_LEAK: document id $DOC in contents of: $out" >&2; bad=1; }
  fi
  return $bad
}
fail() { # a failed build leaves no half-built sandbox
  echo "$1" >&2
  rm -rf "$SBT"
  exit 2
}
resolve_rel() { # a package path: absolute, else under SRC_REPO when present there, else under REPO
  case "$1" in
    /*) echo "$1" ;;
    *) if [ -e "$SRC_REPO/$1" ]; then echo "$SRC_REPO/$1"; else echo "$REPO/$1"; fi ;;
  esac
}

mkdir -p "$D" "$SB/cand/$DOC"
if [ -d "$TARGET" ]; then
  if masked_ok "$TARGET" && [ -z "$(git -C "$TARGET" status --porcelain 2>&1)" ] && leak_check "$TARGET"; then
    echo "sandbox valid: $TARGET"
  else
    echo "E_SANDBOX_DIRTY: $TARGET" >&2
    exit 2
  fi
else
  rm -rf "$SBT"
  mkdir -p "$SBT"
  if [ "$KIND" = tree ]; then
    tar -C "$TREEDIR" --exclude=./.git -cf - . | tar -x -C "$SBT" || fail "copy of $TREEDIR failed"
  else
    git -C "$SRC_REPO" archive "$BASE" | tar -x -C "$SBT" || fail "archive of $BASE failed"
  fi
  # H4. Raw mode (DD-15) removes only the eval-workspace folders and the ground-truth files.
  if [ "$RAW" = 1 ]; then
    (cd "$SBT" && rm -rf .dev/eval-workspaces) || fail "removal failed"
  else
    (cd "$SBT" && rm -rf .dev/reflect .dev/tasks/done .dev/eval-workspaces .dev/research) || fail "removal failed"
    (cd "$SBT" && find . -name artifacts -type d -prune -exec rm -rf -- {} +) || fail "removal failed"
    (cd "$SBT" && find . -name progress.md -type f -exec rm -f -- {} +) || fail "removal failed"
    for id in "${IDS[@]}"; do

#   --packages  test hook: another packages file; accepted only under /tmp/.

set -u -o pipefail
source "$(dirname "$0")/common.sh"

usage() {
  echo "usage: build-sandbox.sh [--raw] [--packages FILE] <doc>" >&2
  exit 2
}
RAW=0
PKFILE=$SW/config/packages.json
DOC=
while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
  case "$1" in
    --raw) RAW=1 ;;
    --packages)
      shift
      [ $# -gt 0 ] || usage
      PKFILE=$1
      ;;
    -*) usage ;;
    *)
      [ -z "$DOC" ] || usage
      DOC=$1
      ;;
  esac
  shift
done
[ -n "$DOC" ] || usage
[[ $DOC =~ ^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._-]*$ ]] || { echo "E_DOC: bad document id: $DOC" >&2; exit 2; }

  case "$(realpath -m -- "$PKFILE")/" in
    /tmp/?*) ;;
    *) echo "E_OVERRIDE: --packages $PKFILE is outside /tmp/" >&2; exit 2 ;;
  esac
fi
[ -f "$PKFILE" ] || { echo "E_PACKAGES: $PKFILE not found" >&2; exit 2; }
jq -e --arg p "$DOC" '.packages[$p]' "$PKFILE" >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "unknown package $DOC" >&2; exit 2; }

BASE=$(jq -r --arg p "$DOC" '.packages[$p].base // empty' "$PKFILE")

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# build-snapshots.sh [plan-id ...]
# Rebuilds fixtures/recall/<plan>/snapshot/ for each plan: the repository as it was at the plan's base
# commit (the last commit on master before the plan package was created), limited to the DD-5 search scope
# and with .dev/ removed. The snapshot is a throwaway git repository (the extractors run `git grep` in it).
# The snapshot folders are NOT committed; run this script to recreate them. See AUTHORS.md.
#
# DD-5 scope kept: tracked files under tests/, scripts/, docs/; root-level files; change-log style files
# anywhere; the directory of every path the plan or its source names; same-basename copies of named files.
# Never kept: .dev/, .git, dependency folders (node_modules, .venv, venv, .vendor, vendor, site-packages, .tox).
# Reads the repository with git (archive, ls-tree, cat-file); writes only under fixtures/recall/<plan>/snapshot*.
set -u -o pipefail

HERE=$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)
REPO=${SW_SRC_REPO:-$(git -C "$HERE" rev-parse --show-toplevel)}

# plan id -> base commit (also recorded in AUTHORS.md)
declare -A BASES=(
  [TASK-WF-diagnosticRefres-20261109-144413]=933cf3a4f5fd3e4d8cce8f69c9168a2631574179
  [TASK-WF-devGuideRefactor-20261104-135403]=119622e3a78284f83377f920e3858f864ac7e6c6
  [TASK-WF-removeTheAnyIssu-20261102-053741]=d6b02a4bfb5c64f3c7125aaae1e220724d590517
  [TASK-WF-renameTheScIssue-20261104-174359]=9b9497e64b830f735aac2765ebb74ed658d183f1
)

if [ $# -gt 0 ]; then PLANS=("$@"); else mapfile -t PLANS < <(printf '%s\n' "${!BASES[@]}" | sort); fi

W=$(mktemp -d /tmp/recall-snap.XXXXXXXX) || exit 2
trap 'rm -rf "$W"' EXIT

build_one() {
  local plan=$1 base out tmp n
  base=${BASES[$plan]:-}
  [ -n "$base" ] || { echo "unknown plan $plan" >&2; return 2; }
  [ -f "$HERE/$plan/original.md" ] || { echo "no plan folder $plan" >&2; return 2; }
  git -C "$REPO" rev-parse --verify -q "$base^{commit}" >/dev/null || { echo "E_BASE: $base is not a commit in $REPO" >&2; return 2; }
  out=$HERE/$plan/snapshot
  tmp=$HERE/$plan/snapshot.tmp
  rm -rf -- "$tmp" "$out"

  git -C "$REPO" ls-tree -r --name-only "$base" >"$W/all.txt" || return 2
  # path-like tokens (with a slash) named in the plan or its source
  cat "$HERE/$plan/original.md" "$HERE/$plan/source.md" | grep -oE '[A-Za-z0-9_.-]+(/[A-Za-z0-9_.-]+)+' | sort -u >"$W/tokens.txt"

  awk -v tokfile="$W/tokens.txt" '
    function dirname(p) { return (p ~ /\//) ? gensub(/\/[^\/]*$/, "", 1, p) : "" }
    function basename(p) { return gensub(/^.*\//, "", 1, p) }
    BEGIN {
      while ((getline t < tokfile) > 0) {
        sub(/\/+$/, "", t)
        if (t == "" || t ~ /^\.dev(\/|$)/) continue
        tok[t] = 1
        tokdir[dirname(t)] = 1
        tokbase[basename(t)] = 1
      }
    }
    { files[NR] = $0 }
    END {
      for (i = 1; i <= NR; i++) {
        f = files[i]
        if (f ~ /^\.dev\// || f ~ /^\.git\// ) continue
        if (f ~ /(^|\/)(node_modules|\.venv|venv|\.vendor|vendor|site-packages|\.tox)\// ) continue
        keep = 0
        if (f ~ /^(tests|scripts|docs)\//) keep = 1
        else if (f !~ /\//) keep = 1
        else if (toupper(basename(f)) ~ /^(CHANGELOG|CHANGES|HISTORY|NEWS|RELEASE[-_]?NOTES)/) keep = 1
        else if (dirname(f) in tokdir) keep = 1
        else if (basename(f) in tokbase && (basename(f) ~ /\./)) keep = 1
        else {
          # a plan-named directory: keep everything under it
          d = dirname(f)
          while (d != "") { if (d in tok) { keep = 1; break }; d = dirname(d) }
        }
        if (keep) print f
      }
    }' "$W/all.txt" >"$W/keep.txt" || return 2
  n=$(wc -l <"$W/keep.txt")
  [ "$n" -gt 0 ] || { echo "nothing selected for $plan" >&2; return 2; }

  mkdir -p "$tmp" || return 2
  # git archive writes the base tree; tar extracts only the kept names. Names are literal (no globbing).
  git -C "$REPO" archive --format=tar "$base" | tar -x -C "$tmp" --no-recursion --no-wildcards --no-anchored -T "$W/keep.txt" 2>"$W/tar.err"
  if [ "${PIPESTATUS[0]}" -ne 0 ] || [ "${PIPESTATUS[1]}" -ne 0 ]; then
    echo "archive/extract failed for $plan: $(head -3 "$W/tar.err")" >&2
    rm -rf -- "$tmp"; return 2
  fi
  rm -rf -- "$tmp/.dev" "$tmp/.git"
  # the extractors call `git grep`, so the snapshot is its own throwaway git repository
  git -C "$tmp" init -q || return 2
  git -C "$tmp" add -A -f || return 2
  git -C "$tmp" -c user.name=sw -c user.email=sw@localhost -c core.hooksPath=/dev/null -c commit.gpgsign=false commit -q -m "snapshot of $base" || return 2
  mv -- "$tmp" "$out" || return 2
  echo "built $plan/snapshot  base=$base  files=$(git -C "$out" ls-files | wc -l)  size=$(du -sh "$out" | cut -f1)"
}

rc=0
for p in "${PLANS[@]}"; do build_one "$p" || rc=2; done
exit $rc

# anywhere; the directory of every path the plan or its source names; same-basename copies of named files.
# Never kept: .dev/, .git, dependency folders (node_modules, .venv, venv, .vendor, vendor, site-packages, .tox).
# Reads the repository with git (archive, ls-tree, cat-file); writes only under fixtures/recall/<plan>/snapshot*.
set -u -o pipefail

HERE=$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)
REPO=${SW_SRC_REPO:-$(git -C "$HERE" rev-parse --show-toplevel)}

# plan id -> base commit (also recorded in AUTHORS.md)
declare -A BASES=(
  [TASK-WF-diagnosticRefres-20261109-144413]=933cf3a4f5fd3e4d8cce8f69c9168a2631574179
  [TASK-WF-devGuideRefactor-20261104-135403]=119622e3a78284f83377f920e3858f864ac7e6c6
  [TASK-WF-removeTheAnyIssu-20261102-053741]=d6b02a4bfb5c64f3c7125aaae1e220724d590517
  [TASK-WF-renameTheScIssue-20261104-174359]=9b9497e64b830f735aac2765ebb74ed658d183f1
)

if [ $# -gt 0 ]; then PLANS=("$@"); else mapfile -t PLANS < <(printf '%s\n' "${!BASES[@]}" | sort); fi

W=$(mktemp -d /tmp/recall-snap.XXXXXXXX) || exit 2
trap 'rm -rf "$W"' EXIT

build_one() {
  local plan=$1 base out tmp n
  base=${BASES[$plan]:-}
  [ -n "$base" ] || { echo "unknown plan $plan" >&2; return 2; }
  [ -f "$HERE/$plan/original.md" ] || { echo "no plan folder $plan" >&2; return 2; }
  git -C "$REPO" rev-parse --verify -q "$base^{commit}" >/dev/null || { echo "E_BASE: $base is not a commit in $REPO" >&2; return 2; }
  out=$HERE/$plan/snapshot
  tmp=$HERE/$plan/snapshot.tmp
  rm -rf -- "$tmp" "$out"

  git -C "$REPO" ls-tree -r --name-only "$base" >"$W/all.txt" || return 2
  # path-like tokens (with a slash) named in the plan or its source
  cat "$HERE/$plan/original.md" "$HERE/$plan/source.md" | grep -oE '[A-Za-z0-9_.-]+(/[A-Za-z0-9_.-]+)+' | sort -u >"$W/tokens.txt"

  awk -v tokfile="$W/tokens.txt" '
    function dirname(p) { if (p !~ /\//) return ""; sub(/\/[^\/]*$/, "", p); return p }
    function basename(p) { sub(/^.*\//, "", p); return p }
    BEGIN {
      while ((getline t < tokfile) > 0) {
        sub(/\/+$/, "", t)
        if (t == "" || t ~ /^\.dev(\/|$)/) continue
        tok[t] = 1
        tokdir[dirname(t)] = 1
        tokbase[basename(t)] = 1
      }
    }
    { files[NR] = $0 }
    END {
      for (i = 1; i <= NR; i++) {
        f = files[i]
        if (f ~ /^\.dev\// || f ~ /^\.git\// ) continue
        if (f ~ /(^|\/)(node_modules|\.venv|venv|\.vendor|vendor|site-packages|\.tox)\// ) continue
        keep = 0
        if (f ~ /^(tests|scripts|docs)\//) keep = 1
        else if (f !~ /\//) keep = 1
        else if (toupper(basename(f)) ~ /^(CHANGELOG|CHANGES|HISTORY|NEWS|RELEASE[-_]?NOTES)/) keep = 1
        else if (dirname(f) in tokdir) keep = 1
        else if (basename(f) in tokbase && (basename(f) ~ /\./)) keep = 1
        else {
          # a plan-named directory: keep everything under it
          d = dirname(f)
          while (d != "") { if (d in tok) { keep = 1; break }; d = dirname(d) }
        }
        if (keep) print f
      }
    }' "$W/all.txt" >"$W/keep.txt" || return 2
  n=$(wc -l <"$W/keep.txt")
  [ "$n" -gt 0 ] || { echo "nothing selected for $plan" >&2; return 2; }

  mkdir -p "$tmp" || return 2
  # git archive writes the base tree; tar extracts only the kept names. Names are literal (no globbing).
  git -C "$REPO" archive --format=tar "$base" | tar -x -C "$tmp" --no-recursion --no-wildcards --anchored -T "$W/keep.txt" 2>"$W/tar.err"
  if [ "${PIPESTATUS[0]}" -ne 0 ] || [ "${PIPESTATUS[1]}" -ne 0 ]; then
    echo "archive/extract failed for $plan: $(head -3 "$W/tar.err")" >&2
    rm -rf -- "$tmp"; return 2
  fi
  rm -rf -- "$tmp/.dev" "$tmp/.git"
  # the extractors call `git grep`, so the snapshot is its own throwaway git repository
  git -C "$tmp" init -q || return 2
  git -C "$tmp" add -A -f || return 2
  git -C "$tmp" -c user.name=sw -c user.email=sw@localhost -c core.hooksPath=/dev/null -c commit.gpgsign=false commit -q -m "snapshot of $base" || return 2
  mv -- "$tmp" "$out" || return 2
  echo "built $plan/snapshot  base=$base  files=$(git -C "$out" ls-files | wc -l)  size=$(du -sh "$out" | cut -f1)"
}

rc=0
for p in "${PLANS[@]}"; do build_one "$p" || rc=2; done
exit $rc

# Rename the /sc:issue claim summary file to issue-summary.md and pin worker file names against the subagent report-file block

Source: ./source.md
Goal: No file name that an /sc:issue worker is told to write starts with REPORT, SUMMARY, FINDINGS or ANALYSIS (case-insensitive, `.md`), so Claude Code's subagent Write block (error "Subagents should return findings as text, not write report files.") can no longer refuse claim Wave 4; the claim summary is `.dev/issues/<N>/issue-summary.md` everywhere, `/sc:analyze` reports under `<D>/analysis/` are named like `analysis/analyze-<scope>.md`, and a deterministic test pins both.

## Constraints

- No behaviour change other than the file names and the corrected explanation of why they are chosen. Do not touch the minor notes m1 to m7 or N1 to N3.
- Edit only `src/superclaude/...`, `tests/...` and `docs/...` files named in a task; never edit or `git add` anything under `.claude/` (it is regenerated by `make sync-dev`). Leave `.dev/issues/` alone.
- Do not run `/sc:issue --claim` or `--create`, do not spawn the issue-worker agents, make no gh writes, commits or pushes. UV only for Python.
- `.dev/tasks/` is always staged (`git add .dev/tasks`), this package and its `artifacts/` included. Staging is not committing.
- The tool-input paragraph text below is the single exact text used in all three agent files and in `tests/skills/test_issue_worker_agents.py` (`_TOOL_INPUT_PARAGRAPH`); Task 2 and Task 3 use it verbatim:

  "The files you write under `.dev/issues/` (`scout.md`, `accuracy-check.md`, `issue-summary.md`, the reports under `analysis/` such as `analysis/analyze-<scope>.md`, `flags.md`, `flags-t1.md`, `issue-body.md`, `draft-notes.md`) are input files for the orchestrator's next tool calls (`gh --body-file` posts and `/sc:recommend`), not report files. Claude Code refuses a subagent's Write of any `.md` file whose name starts with REPORT, SUMMARY, FINDINGS or ANALYSIS (in upper case), which is why none of these names starts with those words. Writing every file your job names with the Write tool is mandatory; returning its content as text instead is a failure (`E-WORKER-NO-OUTPUT`)."

## Phase 1: Skill package, agents and command use the new names

## Task 1: Rename the summary template and every skill-package reference to issue-summary.md

Before editing, copy each file this task and Task 2 change (`src/superclaude/skills/sc-issue-protocol/SKILL.md`, `refs/claim.md`, `refs/chains.md`, `templates/summary.md`, `templates/claim-comment.md`, `src/superclaude/agents/issue-worker-t1.md`, `issue-worker-t2.md`, `issue-worker-t3.md`, `src/superclaude/commands/issue.md`) unchanged into `./artifacts/pre/` (keep the basename; prefix the template copies with `template-` and the refs copies with `ref-` so no two collide) as the pre-fix evidence used by Task 3.

Then, all under `src/superclaude/skills/sc-issue-protocol/`:

- `SKILL.md`: the templates table row `templates/summary.md` -> `summary.md (claim)` becomes `templates/issue-summary.md` -> `issue-summary.md (claim)`; Wave 4 (step 5 of Claim mode) names `<D>/issue-summary.md` and states that files under `<D>/analysis/` are named like `<D>/analysis/analyze-<scope>.md`, never starting with analysis, report, summary or findings.
- `refs/claim.md`: line 58 (`/sc:analyze` report saved under `<D>/analysis/`) adds the same naming rule; line 59 writes `<D>/issue-summary.md` from `templates/issue-summary.md`; line 79 input becomes `@.dev/issues/<N>/issue-summary.md`; line 88 links to `<D>/issue-summary.md`.
- `refs/chains.md`: line 7 `<S>` = `.dev/issues/<N>/issue-summary.md`; line 28 "filled from `issue-summary.md`"; line 33 `Summary: .dev/issues/<N>/issue-summary.md`.
- `templates/claim-comment.md` line 17: `- Summary: .dev/issues/<N>/issue-summary.md` (keep the code-span style).
- `templates/next-steps.md` line 8: `- Input: @.dev/issues/<N>/issue-summary.md` (keep the code-span style).

# Make the developer guide teach Orca-ready commands, skills and agents (round 3 plan)

Source: ./source.md
Goal: `docs/developer-guide/SuperClaude-Developer-Guide-Commands-Skills-Agents.md` has one new subsection, 7.6, that explains how a command, skill or agent must be written so an Orca coordinator can run it as a worker, and every touchpoint the source lists points to 7.6 under the source's pointer rule. Every worker claim matches `src/superclaude/core/WORKER-CONTRACT.md`, every rollout or rationale claim matches the planning spec and says so, and each list, number and exact string the source names is written out once, in 7.6.

## Constraints

- Only one delivery file changes: `docs/developer-guide/SuperClaude-Developer-Guide-Commands-Skills-Agents.md`. Do not edit `src/superclaude/core/WORKER-CONTRACT.md`, `src/superclaude/core/HOW-WE-WORK.md`, `plugins/superclaude/skills/sc-recommend/refs/HOW-WE-WORK.md`, or any command, skill, agent or test file, and add no new test file. No other file is created or modified anywhere in the repository.
- Allowed sources. #!/usr/bin/env bash
# build-snapshots.sh [plan-id ...]
# Rebuilds fixtures/recall/<plan>/snapshot/ for each plan: the repository as it was at the plan's base
# commit (the last commit on master before the plan package was created), limited to the DD-5 search scope
# and with .dev/ removed. The snapshot is a throwaway git repository (the extractors run `git grep` in it).
# The snapshot folders are NOT committed; run this script to recreate them. See AUTHORS.md.
#
# DD-5 scope kept: tracked files under tests/, scripts/, docs/; root-level files; change-log style files
# anywhere; the directory of every path the plan or its source names; same-basename copies of named files.
# Never kept: .dev/, .git, dependency folders (node_modules, .venv, venv, .vendor, vendor, site-packages, .tox).
# Reads the repository with git (archive, ls-tree, cat-file); writes only under fixtures/recall/<plan>/snapshot*.
set -u -o pipefail

HERE=$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)
REPO=${SW_SRC_REPO:-$(git -C "$HERE" rev-parse --show-toplevel)}

# plan id -> base commit (also recorded in AUTHORS.md)
declare -A BASES=(
  [TASK-WF-diagnosticRefres-20261109-144413]=933cf3a4f5fd3e4d8cce8f69c9168a2631574179
  [TASK-WF-devGuideRefactor-20261104-135403]=119622e3a78284f83377f920e3858f864ac7e6c6
  [TASK-WF-removeTheAnyIssu-20261102-053741]=d6b02a4bfb5c64f3c7125aaae1e220724d590517
  [TASK-WF-renameTheScIssue-20261104-174359]=9b9497e64b830f735aac2765ebb74ed658d183f1
)

if [ $# -gt 0 ]; then PLANS=("$@"); else mapfile -t PLANS < <(printf '%s\n' "${!BASES[@]}" | sort); fi

W=$(mktemp -d /tmp/recall-snap.XXXXXXXX) || exit 2
trap 'rm -rf "$W"' EXIT

build_one() {
  local plan=$1 base out tmp n
  base=${BASES[$plan]:-}
  [ -n "$base" ] || { echo "unknown plan $plan" >&2; return 2; }
  [ -f "$HERE/$plan/original.md" ] || { echo "no plan folder $plan" >&2; return 2; }
  git -C "$REPO" rev-parse --verify -q "$base^{commit}" >/dev/null || { echo "E_BASE: $base is not a commit in $REPO" >&2; return 2; }
  out=$HERE/$plan/snapshot
  tmp=$HERE/$plan/snapshot.tmp
  rm -rf -- "$tmp" "$out"

  git -C "$REPO" ls-tree -r --name-only "$base" >"$W/all.txt" || return 2
  # path-like tokens (with a slash) named in the plan or its source
  cat "$HERE/$plan/original.md" "$HERE/$plan/source.md" | grep -oE '[A-Za-z0-9_.-]+(/[A-Za-z0-9_.-]+)+' | sort -u >"$W/tokens.txt"

  awk -v tokfile="$W/tokens.txt" '
    function dirname(p) { if (p !~ /\//) return ""; sub(/\/[^\/]*$/, "", p); return p }
    function basename(p) { sub(/^.*\//, "", p); return p }
    BEGIN {
      while ((getline t < tokfile) > 0) {
        sub(/\/+$/, "", t)
        if (t == "" || t ~ /^\.dev(\/|$)/) continue
        tok[t] = 1
        tokdir[dirname(t)] = 1
        tokbase[basename(t)] = 1
      }
    }
    { files[NR] = $0 }
    END {
      for (i = 1; i <= NR; i++) {
        f = files[i]
        if (f ~ /^\.dev\// || f ~ /^\.git\// ) continue
        if (f ~ /(^|\/)(node_modules|\.venv|venv|\.vendor|vendor|site-packages|\.tox)\// ) continue
        keep = 0
        if (f ~ /^(tests|scripts|docs)\//) keep = 1
        else if (f !~ /\//) keep = 1
        else if (toupper(basename(f)) ~ /^(CHANGELOG|CHANGES|HISTORY|NEWS|RELEASE[-_]?NOTES)/) keep = 1
        else if (dirname(f) in tokdir) keep = 1
        else if (basename(f) in tokbase && (basename(f) ~ /\./)) keep = 1
        else {
          # a plan-named directory: keep everything under it
          d = dirname(f)
          while (d != "") { if (d in tok) { keep = 1; break }; d = dirname(d) }
        }
        if (keep) print f
      }
    }' "$W/all.txt" >"$W/keep.txt" || return 2
  n=$(wc -l <"$W/keep.txt")
  [ "$n" -gt 0 ] || { echo "nothing selected for $plan" >&2; return 2; }

  mkdir -p "$tmp" || return 2
  # git archive writes the base tree; tar extracts only the kept names. Names are literal (no globbing).
  git -C "$REPO" archive --format=tar "$base" | tar -x -C "$tmp" --no-recursion --no-wildcards --anchored -T "$W/keep.txt" 2>"$W/tar.err"
  ps=("${PIPESTATUS[@]}")
  if [ "${ps[0]}" -ne 0 ] || [ "${ps[1]}" -ne 0 ]; then
    echo "archive/extract failed for $plan: $(head -3 "$W/tar.err")" >&2
    rm -rf -- "$tmp"; return 2
  fi
  rm -rf -- "$tmp/.dev" "$tmp/.git"
  # the extractors call `git grep`, so the snapshot is its own throwaway git repository
  git -C "$tmp" init -q || return 2
  git -C "$tmp" add -A -f || return 2
  git -C "$tmp" -c user.name=sw -c user.email=sw@localhost -c core.hooksPath=/dev/null -c commit.gpgsign=false commit -q -m "snapshot of $base" || return 2
  mv -- "$tmp" "$out" || return 2
  echo "built $plan/snapshot  base=$base  files=$(git -C "$out" ls-files | wc -l)  size=$(du -sh "$out" | cut -f1)"
}

rc=0
for p in "${PLANS[@]}"; do build_one "$p" || rc=2; done
exit $rc

# Minor findings never fail a review; review loops capped at 2 fix cycles (final plan)

Source: ./source.md
Goal: No shipped primitive, CLI default or CLI prompt fails a review on a minor finding or rechecks minors; every review loop outside /sc:implement runs at most 2 fix cycles (3 reviews) and then escalates the open blocking findings to the user instead of passing them; /sc:implement drops its second A2 repair and keeps its own ladder (A3-A5, halt at review 5) as its at-cap escalation under S4, so its worst case stays its own count; static tests pin all of it.

## Constraints

- Final user decisions (restart spec `/tmp/t11b-severity-rule-restart-spec.md`): B1 minor findings are noted and work proceeds, with no recheck and no FAIL; at the cap, open blocking findings are escalated to the user, never passed; B2 the cap is 2 fix cycles = at most 3 reviews; B3 `/sc:implement` option A; `update.sh` is not changed; cli-portify default 1 iteration (coordinator, inventory section 4 item 3a). Evidence: `/home/coder/workspaces/IronClaude/.dev/worktrees/qa-loop-investigation/.dev/qa-loop-investigation/FINDINGS.md` sections 4 and 5.
- Amendment, user decision 2026-11-02 08:41 UTC (coordinator message msg_9d0fe67f82c7, reply to the review-cap escalation): the 10 open blocking findings of pre-review 3 (`.dev/reflect/pre-removeTheAnyIssu-20261102054021/REPORT.md`, B3-01..B3-10) are added to this plan and it is implemented with no fourth plan review. Safeguards: (1) one fixed, recorded site sweep, `.dev/review-severity-rule/site-sweep.md` (pattern list, every hit, and for each hit its task or the reason it is not a rule of this kind); its literal edits for sites outside the earlier lists are `.dev/review-severity-rule/sweep-edits.yaml` (Task 19); (2) the static test of Task 20 fails if any swept wording survives as a rule; (3) acceptance checks use text anchors, not line numbers (B3-09). Per-task QA and the FINAL review stay as they are, each under the 2-fix-cycle cap. This amendment was made by hand on the user's instruction; it is the one exception to never editing a generated plan from reflect findings.
- This plan replaces packages `TASK-WF-removeTheAnyIssu-20261101-225635` and `TASK-WF-removeTheAnyIssu-20261102-042031`; their pre-review findings (B-01..B-11, P2-B1..P2-B7) are folded in.
- Site lists (repo-relative): severity wording `.dev/review-severity-rule/inventory.md` sections 1, 2, 4 and 6; every cap and at-cap edit `.dev/review-severity-rule/cap-edits.yaml` (161 rows with literal `old` and `new`, grouped `agents`, `templates`, `skills-a`, `skills-b`, `portify`, `prd-core`; a row with `occurrences` > 1 is applied to every occurrence). Severity line numbers are against `f90877be`; locate each site by its quoted text.
- CAP_CHECK for a group G (run from the repo root): `uv run python -I -c 'import sys,yaml,pathlib; rows=[r for r in yaml.safe_load(open(".dev/review-severity-rule/cap-edits.yaml"))["rows"] if r["group"]==sys.argv[1]]; bad=[r["id"] for r in rows if r["old"] in pathlib.Path(r["file"]).read_text() or r["new"] not in pathlib.Path(r["file"]).read_text()]; print(len(rows), "rows; failing:", bad); sys.exit(1 if bad else 0)' G`. It exits 0 only when every row of the group has its `old` absent and its `new` present.

Copies of S1-S5 are taken from `.dev/review-severity-rule/inventory.md` section 1 (no "(S1)".."(S5)" labels, no S3 annotation). # Minor findings never fail a review; review loops capped at 2 fix cycles (final plan)

Goal: No shipped primitive, CLI default or CLI prompt fails a review on a minor finding or rechecks minors; every review loop outside /sc:implement runs at most 2 fix cycles (3 reviews) and then escalates the open blocking findings to the user instead of passing them; /sc:implement drops its second A2 repair and keeps its own ladder (A3-A5, halt at review 5) as its at-cap escalation under S4, so its worst case stays its own count; static tests pin all of it.

# Recall fixture repair (Sweep Sheet freeze check), 2026-11-15

Context for a reader with no history: the first freeze check (`results/freeze-check-20261115.md`) failed, and named two fixture gaps: the four recall plans had no `snapshot/` (so the evidence-searching extractors had nothing to search) and class C8 had one seed. This repair closes both gaps. It changes no extractor and was done by a fresh Sonnet session (claude-sonnet-5-5) that had not read the extractors or any ground truth and knew the first failing result. Nothing was run on the extractors, so this note says nothing about recall.

## Files created or changed (all under `fixtures/recall/` except this report)

| File | What |
|---|---|
| `build-snapshots.sh` (new, executable) | Rebuilds `<plan>/snapshot/` for all four plans, or for plan ids given as arguments. About 8 seconds for all four. |
| `<plan>/snapshot/` x4 (new, untracked) | DD-5 scope of the repository at the base commit, `.dev/` removed, a throwaway git repository inside. 30 to 45 MB each, about 155 MB in all. |
| `.gitignore` (new) | Lists `*/snapshot/` so a stray `git add` skips the snapshots (each has a nested `.git`). Not asked for; added to keep the "never commit" rule from depending on memory. |
| `TASK-WF-removeTheAnyIssu-20261102-053741/seeds.json` | Seeds s12 to s15 added (class C8, each with a `note` field naming the pinned file). The first 11 seeds are byte-identical in content. |
| `TASK-WF-removeTheAnyIssu-20261102-053741/seeded.md` | One edit: the Constraints note that named `docs/guides/tdd-skill-release-guide.md` (as out of scope) was removed, which creates seed s12. |
| `AUTHORS.md` | Seed counts, base shas, snapshot section, repair section, C8 limits, the second-author statement. |

## Base shas

| Plan | Base commit |
|---|---|
| `TASK-WF-diagnosticRefres-20261109-144413` | `94e609ccef2a5ee67fa8918426157046be1f32c8` |
| `TASK-WF-devGuideRefactor-20261104-135403` | `8db29f1165508187b7a14a48f2f66793e269d596` (feature branch commit; the plan names `WORKER-CONTRACT.md` and `test_worker_contract.py`, which master at that date does not hold) |
| `TASK-WF-removeTheAnyIssu-20261102-053741` | `d6b02a4bfb5c64f3c7125aaae1e220724d590517` |
| `TASK-WF-renameTheScIssue-20261104-174359` | `b5c09e90e6584c4bb8b340723f4008ffb21b3460` |

How chosen: the latest commit on any branch before the UTC timestamp in the plan's folder name (read as UTC because the implement ledgers of all four plans start after it in UTC), except `devGuideRefactor`, where an earlier commit holds all 8 existing files the plan names and the latest does not. The ledger "start sha" values in the plan packages are tree hashes, not commits, so they were not usable. My first choice (last commit on master) was wrong for `devGuideRefactor`, `diagnosticRefres` and `renameTheScIssue`; I found that by counting the plan-named files present at each candidate and rebuilt.

## Seed counts per class (41 in all, was 37)

C1 5, C2 7, C4 6, C5 5, C6 6, C7 7, **C8 5 (was 1)**. Per plan: diagnosticRefres 7, devGuideRefactor 12, removeTheAnyIssu 15 (was 11), renameTheScIssue 7. Every one of the 41 quotes occurs exactly once in its `seeded.md` (checked with `grep -o -F`).

## The four new C8 seeds (all in removeTheAnyIssu; pinned file shown in each seed's `note`)

| Seed | Plan sentence quoted | Pinned by (in the snapshot) | Kind |
|---|---|---|---|
| s12 | Task 7, tdd build-request-template "lines 124 and 152" | `docs/guides/tdd-skill-release-guide.md:345` ("Zero leniency ...") and `:271` | inserted (original out-of-scope note for this guide removed) |
| s13 | Task 7, prd build-request-template "lines 129 and 157" | `docs/guides/prd-skill-release-guide.md:332` and `:261` | located |
| s14 | Task 17, `models.py:203` `max_research_fix_cycles` | `docs/guides/prd-skill-release-guide.md:455` ("max 3 for research") | located |
| s15 | Task 2, "the research-gate Verdict bullets (171-172)" | `docs/reference/nfr-conv-2-prose-determinism.md:131-133` (quotes the rf-qa gate rule) | located |

Each pin was confirmed with `git grep` in the snapshot, and the plan names none of these documents (the plan never says `prd-skill-release-guide`, `nfr-conv-2` or `docs/reference`).

## What I could not do, and what you should decide

1. **Only 1 of 4 C8 seeds is an inserted edit.** s13, s14 and s15 are defects the original plan already had (it edits something a document pins and never names the document); I located and verified them but did not edit the plan text for them. `AUTHORS.md` says so. This is a real departure from "seeds are additions". If you want inserted seeds only, drop s13 to s15; C8 then has 2 seeds (s11, s12), still below 5.
2. **No other plan can hold C8 seeds.** `diagnosticRefres` edits no repository file (it refreshes an installed skill). `devGuideRefactor` edits only the developer guide, and `git grep` finds no test or document outside the tests the plan runs that pins it. `renameTheScIssue` edits `/sc:issue` files that were untracked when the plan was written (first committed in `6542ca72b` together with the plan's own work), so no snapshot can hold them and its evidence searches will find nothing; its snapshot is a valid tree but a weak fixture for E2 to E4.
3. **C8 recall rests on one plan.** All five C8 seeds are in removeTheAnyIssu, and four of them are pinned by documents, not tests (the plan already runs every test directory that pins its edits, so no further test pin was found). s11 is pinned by a test in a directory the plan runs (`tests/audit`), without naming that file, so under the strict "never names or runs" reading s11 is the weakest C8 seed. I did not change it.
4. **Snapshots are untracked and big.** They must be rebuilt (`fixtures/recall/build-snapshots.sh`) on any other checkout before the `freeze` tests. The `.gitignore` also hides them from `git status`.
5. **Search scope.** The DD-5 scope is implemented in the script (tests/, scripts/, docs/, root files, change-log files, directories of plan-named paths, same-basename copies, no `.dev/` or dependency folders). It pulls in some `src/` and `plugins/` files through plan-named directories. If the extractor's scope function is stricter, the snapshots hold more than it reads, which is harmless.
6. **Not done:** no extractor, freeze test or lint was run; no overlap check against the hold-out set; nothing was staged or committed.

## Recommended next step

Re-run the freeze check with the snapshots in place before changing any extractor, and read the E2, E3 and E4 numbers against the missing-snapshot explanation in the first result. Treat any C8 figure as a single-plan figure.
